A deviation not listed in Form 4-E will be taken as accepted.”; VOL-V:29.2 p3: “The Availability Payment shall be indexed annually in accordance with Schedule 9”; VOL-V:31.2 p3: “the Authority shall deduct from the Availability Payment the amounts calculated under Schedule 7”; VOL-V:39.1 p4: “being the events listed in Schedule 11”; VOL-V:39.5 p4: “the notice and cure period stated in the Direct Agreement”; VOL-V:40.1 p4: “calculated under Schedule 12”

rows.already_settled: ADD-02 Q7: the order of precedence in VOL-I 3.2 applies and no amendment is considered necessary; under 3.2(b)-(c) Volume I prevails over Volume V, so for the RFP Documents the concession runs 25 years from PCOD. That is not re-asked.
rows.clause: Section 6, response to question 7 (Volume I Clause 12.1; Volume V Clauses 3.1 and 42.2)
rows.gap: ADD-02 Q7 directs Bidders to precedence, under which Volume I (12.1: 25 years from PCOD) prevails over Volume V (3.1: 25 years from the Effective Date), but Volume V is left unamended. Still open: whether VOL-V 3.1 left unlisted in Form 4-E would be 'taken as accepted' under the Volume V Note, and how 'the term' in VOL-V 3.2 and 42.2 is to be read.
rows.interim_handling: Base the Financial Model on VOL-I 12.1 as the Q7 precedence answer directs (25 years of operation from PCOD) and run a sensitivity on the VOL-V 3.1 reading. Legal decides whether also to record VOL-V 3.1 in Form 4-E as a protective entry citing VOL-I 12.1 and ADD-02 Q7.
rows.practical_impact: The readings differ by the construction period (36 months from Notice to Proceed, VOL-V 12.1, plus any time from the Effective Date), changing the years of Availability Payment, debt tenor, the year-20 handback reserve trigger and the handback date; the Financial Model and Form 4-E depend on it.
rows.proposed_question: Addendum No. 2, response to question 7, page 2; Volume V, Clauses 3.1 (page 2) and 42.2 (page 4): Further to the Authority's response that the order of precedence in Volume I Clause 3.2 applies to the concession term, will a Bidder that does not list Volume V Clause 3.1 in Form 4-E be taken, under the Note to Bidders in Volume V, to have accepted a term running from the Effective Date, and is 'the term' in Volume V Clauses 3.2 and 42.2 to be read as the twenty-five (25) year period commencing on PCOD stated in Volume I Clause 12.1 (page 6)?
rows.sources: ADD-02:Q7 p2: “The order of precedence at Volume I Clause 3.2 applies. The Authority does not consider further amendment necessary at this stage.”; VOL-I:12.1 p6: “The concession period shall be twenty-five (25) years commencing on the Project Commercial Operation Date”; VOL-V:3.1 p2: “shall continue for a period of twenty-five (25) years from the Effective Date”; VOL-V:42.2 p4: “A handback reserve shall be funded from the start of year twenty (20) of the term”; VOL-V:cover/note-to-bidders p2: “A deviation not listed in Form 4-E will be taken as accepted.”

rows.already_settled: ADD-02 Q11 settles that Bidders design to the Volume II figures: the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day) and peak hourly flow (7,500 m³/h, a peaking factor of 1.5 on the 5,000 m³/h average) stand, are not contradictory and are not re-asked. Q11 did not address row 2-6.4 or define DWF; VOL-II 4.2 itself asks Bidders to raise flow inconsistencies under VOL-I 5.1.
rows.gap: 'Dry weather flow' is not defined. If it equals the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day, i.e. 5,000 m³/h), the storm flow to be passed to full treatment (3 x DWF, 15,000 m³/h) is twice the peak hourly design flow of 7,500 m³/h used for the hydraulic profile and the transmission main (VOL-II 4.1, 5.2), so the governing storm design flow is unclear.
rows.interim_handling: Design to the stated Table 2-6 figures and carry the more onerous reading (3 x average daily flow, 15,000 m³/h, through inlet works and full treatment) as the hydraulic case, with the 7,500 m³/h case costed as a variant. Record the assumption in the design basis; add no qualification to the Proposal.
rows.practical_impact: Sets the hydraulic capacity of the inlet works, treatment streams and channels and possibly of the transmission main and reservoir; a two-fold difference in storm design flow is a major capex and footprint item and bears on meeting Table 2-4 under storm conditions.
rows.proposed_question: Volume II, Table 2-6, row 2-6.4, page 4: How is 'dry weather flow' in row 2-6.4 defined, and what storm flow, in m³/h, is to be passed to full treatment and accommodated by the hydraulic profile under Clause 4.1 (page 3), given that three times a dry weather flow equal to the average daily flow in row 2-6.1 (120,000 m³/day) would exceed the peak hourly flow (design) of 7,500 m³/h in row 2-6.2?
rows.sources: VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.4 p4: “Storm flow to be passed to full treatment”; VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.4 p4: “3 x dry weather flow”; VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.1 p3: “Average daily flow | Value: 120,000 | Unit: m³/day”; VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.2 p3: “Peak hourly flow (design) | Value: 7,500 | Unit: m³/h”; VOL-II:4.1 p3: “The hydraulic profile shall accommodate the flows in Table 2-6 without surcharge of any structure and without reliance on pumped bypass.”; ADD-02:Q11 p2: “Bidders shall design to the figures stated in Volume II. Volume II Clause 4.2 applies.”

rows.already_settled: ADD-02 5.1 sets TN at 3 mg/l on the same basis for the RFP Documents (an Addendum prevails, VOL-I 3.2(a)), superseding the original 5 mg/l reading. The minutes' remark that the permit was under review (ADD-01 Appendix B item 5) does not bind (ADD-01 3.2). Re-read at ADD-03 (blind rehearsal 03, 1 Nov 2026): ADD-03 5.1 sets TP at 0.5 mg/l, unit and basis unchanged, and states that all other entries (TN as amended by ADD-02) are unchanged; it says nothing about the Permit.
rows.gap: The Environmental Permit is not among the RFP Documents, yet it prevails over the Table 2-4 reproduction (VOL-II page 3 preamble) and, by Note 1, sets the limits for any parameter not listed. Bidders cannot see those limits or check the reproduction, and whether the Permit reflects the ADD-02 TN amendment, or the ADD-03 TP amendment (1 to 0.5 mg/l), is not stated.
rows.interim_handling: Design to Table 2-4 as amended (TN 3 mg/l and TP 0.5 mg/l, each on the 30-day rolling-average basis) and make no claim of Permit compliance, including for the TN and TP amendments. Record unlisted-parameter limits as an open design risk; completing the bid does not depend on receiving the Permit.
rows.practical_impact: Unknown limits for unlisted parameters, and any Permit value stricter than the reproduction, bear on process design (criterion A, 25 marks), the performance risk priced into the Availability Payment and possibly Unavailability Events under VOL-V 31.1(b), which have no cure period. Permit compliance cannot be claimed.
rows.proposed_question: Volume II, Clause 2.4 (page 2) and Table 2-4, Note 1 (page 3): Table 2-4 is reproduced from the Environmental Permit, which is stated to prevail in any discrepancy, and Note 1 applies the Permit's limits to any parameter not listed. The Permit has not been issued with the RFP Documents. Will the Authority issue the Environmental Permit or, failing that, state the limits and bases of assessment it sets for parameters not listed in Table 2-4, and is the Permit consistent with Table 2-4 as amended by Addendum No. 2, Section 5.1 (page 1) and Addendum No. 3, Section 5.1 (page 2)?
rows.sources: VOL-II:2.4 p2: “Table 2-4 is reproduced overleaf from the Environmental Permit issued for the site and is incorporated into this Volume by reference.”; VOL-II:T2-4-heading/para1 p3: “In the event of any discrepancy between this reproduction and the Environmental Permit, the Environmental Permit shall prevail.”; VOL-II:T2-4/note1 p3: “Where a parameter is not listed above, the limit stated in the Environmental Permit shall apply.”; ADD-02:5.1 p1: “the limit for Total Nitrogen (TN) is amended from the value shown to 3 mg/l, assessed on the same basis.”; ADD-03:5.1 p2: “in the row for Total Phosphorus (TP), the limit is amended from 1 mg/l to 0.5 mg/l”

rows.already_settled: ADD-01 Q1 settles that no process train is mandated but does not address disinfection residuals. The printed qualifier and each row's basis of assessment are as read and confirmed; nothing settles the ranges. Re-read at ADD-03 (blind rehearsal 03, 1 Nov 2026): ADD-03 5.1 amends only the TP limit and states that all other entries in Table 2-4 are unchanged; it does not address the ranges or the qualifier, so the question stands.
rows.clause: Table 2-4 (Residual Chlorine and pH rows), with Clause 3.3
rows.gap: Residual Chlorine (0.5 - 1.0 mg/l) and pH (6.0 - 9.0) are printed as ranges under a qualifier that 'all values are maxima'. If 0.5 mg/l is a minimum residual at the outlet, ultraviolet-only disinfection and dechlorination, both permitted by VOL-II 3.3, could not comply; if it is not, the lower figures have no stated function.
rows.interim_handling: Treat both ranges as two-sided limits for design and provide the ability to hold a 0.5 - 1.0 mg/l chlorine residual at the outlet whatever primary disinfection is selected; keep each parameter's printed basis of assessment.
rows.practical_impact: Determines whether a chlorine dosing and residual-control system is required at the outlet whatever disinfection method is chosen, and how continuously monitored failures arise (VOL-II 2.5; VOL-V 31.1(b), no cure period).
rows.proposed_question: Volume II, Table 2-4 and Clause 3.3, page 3: Table 2-4 states that all values are maxima, but gives Residual Chlorine as 0.5 - 1.0 mg/l and pH as 6.0 - 9.0, each assessed 'Continuous at outlet'. Are the lower values (0.5 mg/l Residual Chlorine and pH 6.0) minimum limits and, if a minimum chlorine residual applies, does it apply where disinfection is by ultraviolet irradiation alone or by chlorination with dechlorination as permitted by Clause 3.3?
rows.sources: VOL-II:T2-4 p3: “(all values are maxima; compliance assessed as a 30-day rolling average unless stated)”; VOL-II:T2-4/ResidualChlorine p3: “Limit: 0.5 - 1.0 | Basis of assessment: Continuous at outlet”; VOL-II:T2-4/pH p3: “Limit: 6.0 - 9.0 | Basis of assessment: Continuous at outlet”; VOL-II:3.3 p3: “Disinfection shall be by chlorination with provision for dechlorination, or by ultraviolet irradiation with a validated dose, or by a combination.”

rows.gap: Volume III (Drawings), listed as an RFP Document, has not been issued. The effluent delivery point is identified only by Drawing 03-C-114, and the 'two designated tie-in points' to the collection network are not identified in any document issued.
rows.interim_handling: Design and price the main on the stated parameters (about 18 km, minimum DN1200, maximum 2.0 m/s, 15 m residual head) with the delivery point, route and tie-in locations as labelled assumptions and a cost allowance; completing the bid does not depend on receiving Volume III.
rows.practical_impact: The delivery point fixes the route and length of the approximately 18 km main and the pumping head for 15 m residual head (VOL-II 5.2), which is also an Unavailability Event test (VOL-V 31.1(c)); the tie-in points fix the interface and temporary works (VOL-II 1.3). Omission claims close at the Proposal Due Date (VOL-I 3.4).
rows.proposed_question: Volume II, Clause 5.1, page 4, and Clause 1.3, page 2: Volume I Clause 3.1 (page 2) lists Volume III (Drawings) as an RFP Document, but Volume III has not been issued. Will the Authority issue Volume III or, failing that, state the location and ground level of the delivery point shown on Drawing 03-C-114 and the location of the two designated tie-in points referred to in Clause 1.3?
rows.sources: VOL-I:3.1 p2: “Volume III (Drawings)”; VOL-II:5.1 p4: “between the Facility outlet chamber and the delivery point shown on Drawing 03-C-114”; VOL-II:5.2 p4: “a minimum residual head of 15 m at the delivery point”; VOL-II:1.3 p2: “at the two designated tie-in points”; VOL-I:3.4 p3: “No claim arising from an alleged omission shall be entertained after the Proposal Due Date.”

rows.already_settled: ADD-02 Q13 settles that the 12.2 periods (Commercial Close 120 days, Financial Close 270 days from the Preferred Bidder Notification) are unchanged; ADD-02 Q8 and ADD-01 Q3 settle the bond amount and issuer. None of these is re-asked.
rows.gap: The Bid Bond runs 180 days from the Proposal Due Date (to about 25 May 2027) and must be extended only when Proposal validity is extended, but VOL-I 12.2 lets the Authority call it if Financial Close is missed, up to 270 days after the Preferred Bidder Notification (as late as about January 2028 if notification comes at the end of the 150-day validity). No clause requires the bond to cover that period.
rows.interim_handling: Arrange the bond to VOL-I 6.3-6.4 with an expiry no earlier than the later counting reading (25 May 2027), and obtain the bank's indicative agreement to extend it through a Financial Close long-stop; carry that extension cost in the bid budget without assuming the Authority's answer.
rows.practical_impact: Determines the expiry date and extension commitment the issuing bank must give, and its cost, and the Preferred Bidder's exposure to a call at Financial Close; a fixed-expiry bank instrument must be drafted to match.
rows.proposed_question: Volume I, Clause 6.3, page 3, and Clause 12.2, page 6: Clause 6.3 requires the Bid Bond to remain valid for 180 days from the Proposal Due Date, extended where Proposal validity is extended, while Clause 12.2 entitles the Authority to call the Bid Bond if Financial Close is not achieved by the long-stop date, which may fall up to 270 days after the Preferred Bidder Notification. Will the Preferred Bidder be required to extend the Bid Bond so that it remains valid until Financial Close or the long-stop date and, if so, to what date?
rows.sources: VOL-I:6.3 p3: “shall remain valid for one hundred and eighty (180) days from the Proposal Due Date and shall be extended on demand where the Authority extends the period of Proposal validity”; VOL-I:12.2 p6: “Failure to achieve Financial Close by the long-stop date entitles the Authority to call the Bid Bond and to proceed with the next ranked Bidder.”; VOL-I:12.2 p6: “Financial Close within two hundred and seventy (270) days, of the date of the Preferred Bidder Notification”; ADD-02:Q13 p2: “The periods in Volume I Clause 12.2 are unchanged.”

rows.already_settled: Re-read at ADD-03 (blind rehearsal 03, 1 Nov 2026): ADD-03 6.2 deletes VOL-V 31.4 in its entirety and 39.3 with it (Clauses not renumbered), and Q18 answers a question on the 31.4 rolling period: 'Volume V Clause 31.4 is deleted by Section 6.2 of this Addendum. The question does not arise.' Persistent breach and its termination right are gone, so (a)-(c) no longer arise. Before ADD-03: ADD-02 Q12 refers Bidders to 31.2: deductions are uncapped. The 29.3 Ramp-Up exception removes availability deductions only, for rolling-average parameters; it is not an exemption from technical compliance or commissioning and is not re-asked.
rows.gap: Clause 31.4 does not say how Unavailability Events are counted where a failure continues (for example a 30-day rolling-average exceedance lasting several days, with no cure period), whether events in the Ramp-Up Period that attract no deduction under 29.3 still count, or what 'a second occurrence' refers to (a second persistent breach, or a further event after the remediation plan).
rows.interim_handling: Re-read at ADD-03 (blind rehearsal 03, 1 Nov 2026): not to be raised (answered by ADD-03 6.2 and Q18). Before ADD-03: Assess risk on the strictest reading (each day of a continuing failure an event; Ramp-Up events counted) and set process design margins accordingly; Legal decides whether a Form 4-E entry is needed. Schedule 7, which is not issued, may bear on the answer.
rows.practical_impact: Re-read at ADD-03 (blind rehearsal 03, 1 Nov 2026): none remains for persistent breach; Unavailability Events still attract uncapped deductions (31.2) with no cure period for a Table 2-4 failure (31.3). Before ADD-03: On the strictest counting a single multi-day rolling-average excursion could reach three events and, on a second occurrence, a termination right under 39.3 with compensation on Project Company default (40.2); this drives process margins, lender due diligence and possibly a Form 4-E entry.
rows.proposed_question: Volume V, Clause 31.4, page 3: (a) How are Unavailability Events under Clause 31.1(b) counted for the purposes of Clause 31.4 where a failure of a Table 2-4 parameter assessed as a 30-day rolling average continues over more than one day; (b) do events occurring during the Ramp-Up Period, for which Clause 29.3 provides that no availability deduction applies, count towards a persistent breach; and (c) does 'a second occurrence' mean a second persistent breach as defined in Clause 31.4?
rows.sources: VOL-V:31.4 p3: “Persistent breach, being three (3) or more Unavailability Events in any rolling ninety (90) day period, entitles the Authority to require a remediation plan and, on a second occurrence, to terminate under Clause 39.3.”; VOL-V:31.1 p3: “(b) the treated effluent fails any parameter in Volume II Table 2-4”; VOL-V:31.3 p3: “No cure period applies to an event under Clause 31.1(b).”; VOL-V:29.3 p3: “no availability deduction shall apply to a parameter listed in Table 2-4 as assessed on a rolling average basis”

rows.gap: Most Table 2-4 parameters are assessed as 30-day rolling averages, but VOL-II 7.2-7.3 do not say how such a parameter is 'met', or what counts as 'a failure', within a 30-day run: an average over the run, a daily rolling value using pre-run data, or individual samples.
rows.interim_handling: Plan commissioning so that individual samples meet the rolling-average limits before the run starts, and hold programme float for at least one full restart; record this as a programme assumption.
rows.practical_impact: A failure restarts the full 30 days; PCOD timing drives delay liquidated damages of SAR 180,000 per day (VOL-V 18.1) and the 365-day termination right (VOL-V 18.3), so the commissioning programme and float depend on the answer.
rows.proposed_question: Volume II, Clauses 7.2 and 7.3, page 4: For Table 2-4 parameters whose basis of assessment is a 30-day rolling average, how is compliance determined during the 30-day reliability run (in particular, is the rolling average calculated over the run period only, or for each day of the run using data from before it began), and what constitutes 'a failure' of such a parameter for the purposes of Clause 7.3?
rows.sources: VOL-II:7.2 p4: “PCOD shall not be certified until the Facility has completed a continuous reliability run of thirty (30) days at not less than 90% of nominal capacity, during which every parameter in Table 2-4 has been met.”; VOL-II:7.3 p4: “A failure of any Table 2-4 parameter during the reliability run shall restart the run in full.”; VOL-II:T2-4 p3: “compliance assessed as a 30-day rolling average unless stated”; VOL-V:18.1 p2: “delay liquidated damages at the rate of SAR 180,000 for each day of delay”

rows.already_settled: ADD-02 2.1 sets the limit at 150 A4 pages (replacing 120); ADD-01 Q2 settles that it applies to the narrative only and that Form Sheets are excluded (its '120-page' wording is stale, its substance stands).
rows.gap: The page limit excludes 'the appendices expressly permitted by Volume II', but Volume II as issued (Sections 1 to 9) does not expressly permit any appendix, so it is unclear whether any supporting material (for example the lifecycle plan, the whole-life cost comparison under VOL-II 5.3 / ADD-01 5.1, or ESMP material under VOL-II 9.1) falls outside the limit.
rows.interim_handling: Plan the narrative so that all technical content other than the Form Sheets and the separate items listed in VOL-I 9.1 fits within 150 A4 pages; keep any appendix material ready to move inside the limit if none is permitted.
rows.practical_impact: Pages over the limit are removed and not scored (9.2), and the technical score must reach 70 marks to proceed (VOL-I 11.3; ADD-02 note (1)); page planning of the Technical Proposal depends on it.
rows.proposed_question: Volume I, Clause 9.2, page 5 (as amended by Addendum No. 2, Section 2.1): Which appendices are 'expressly permitted by Volume II' and so excluded from the 150-page limit, given that no such appendix is identified in Volume II as issued, or are no appendices so permitted?
rows.sources: VOL-I:9.2 p5: “excluding the Form Sheets and the appendices expressly permitted by Volume II. Pages in excess of the limit will be removed before evaluation and will not be scored.”; ADD-02:2.1 p1: “one hundred and fifty (150) pages”; ADD-01:Q2 p1: “The limit applies to the Technical Proposal narrative only. Form Sheets and the appendices permitted by Volume II are excluded.”

rows.already_settled: ADD-02 note (2) sets the weighting at 65% technical / 35% commercial, replacing VOL-I 11.2 (60/40); the minutes' 'seventy / thirty' remark does not bind (ADD-01 3.2). Note (1) keeps the 70-mark threshold, and the revised marks (B 15, D 20, total 100) are settled.
rows.clause: Section 3, Note (3) to revised Table 1-1 (with Volume I Clauses 11.2 and 11.3)
rows.gap: Note (3) introduces 'the Authority's standard five-point scale' multiplied by 'the weight shown', but the scale is not in the pack and the revised table shows marks, not weights, so how a criterion score becomes marks out of 100 (and is tested against the 70-mark threshold) is not stated. No method is given anywhere for calculating the commercial score.
rows.interim_handling: Write to the revised marks per criterion (A 25, B 15, C 20, D 20, E 10, F 10) and aim for a clear margin above 70; treat the commercial formula as unknown and test price sensitivity without assuming one.
rows.practical_impact: Determines how the technical narrative is weighted across criteria, the margin needed above the 70-mark threshold (below it Envelope B is returned unopened, VOL-I 11.3), and how price translates into the 35% commercial score.
rows.proposed_question: Addendum No. 2, Section 3, Note (3) to revised Table 1-1, page 1: (a) What is the Authority's standard five-point scale, and how is a score on that scale converted into the marks shown in revised Table 1-1, including for the 70-mark threshold in Volume I Clause 11.3 (page 5), given that the table shows marks rather than weights? (b) By what method is the commercial score calculated for the 35% commercial weighting?
rows.sources: ADD-02:T1-1-rev/note(3) p1: “Marks are awarded on the Authority's standard five-point scale and multiplied by the weight shown.”; ADD-02:T1-1-rev p1: “Ref | Criterion | Marks”; ADD-02:T1-1-rev/note(2) p1: “is amended to sixty-five per cent (65%) technical and thirty-five per cent (35%) commercial.”; VOL-I:11.3 p5: “A Proposal scoring less than seventy (70) marks out of one hundred (100) at the technical evaluation shall not proceed to commercial evaluation”

rows.gap: VOL-V 42.1 takes the handback condition from VOL-II 8.5, which provides only for a survey and remedial works and states no condition standard or who identifies the works, while VOL-II 1.1 points back to Volume V. 'Major assets', to which the five-year remaining design life applies, is not defined.
rows.interim_handling: Plan lifecycle replacements so that civil structures and all significant mechanical and electrical assets have at least five years' remaining design life at handback (a labelled planning assumption), and fund the reserve from year 20 of the term on the term reading used in the Financial Model.
rows.practical_impact: Sets the lifecycle replacement profile in the final concession years, the handback reserve funded from year 20 (VOL-V 42.2) and the lifecycle cost in the Availability Payment; criterion C (lifecycle strategy, 20 marks) also depends on it.
rows.proposed_question: Volume V, Clause 42.1, page 4: Clause 42.1 requires transfer 'in the condition required by Volume II Clause 8.5' with a remaining design life of not less than five years for all major assets, but Volume II Clause 8.5 (page 5) provides for a condition survey and remedial works without stating a condition standard, and Volume II Clause 1.1 (page 2) refers back to Volume V. Against what condition standard will the handback survey and remedial works be assessed, and what are the 'major assets' for the purposes of Clause 42.1?
rows.sources: VOL-V:42.1 p4: “in the condition required by Volume II Clause 8.5, free of encumbrance and with a remaining design life of not less than five (5) years for all major assets”; VOL-II:8.5 p5: “A handback condition survey shall be carried out in the final two (2) years of the concession, and any remedial works identified shall be completed before transfer.”; VOL-II:1.1 p2: “shall transfer the Facility to the Authority at the end of the concession period in the condition required by Volume V”

rows.already_settled: ADD-02 Q10 settles that the guarantee is required only from the ultimate parent of the EPC Contractor, not the O&M Operator; not re-asked.
rows.clause: Form 4-D (guaranteed obligations and expiry), with Volume I Clause 8.7
rows.gap: The guarantee covers the EPC Contractor's obligations 'during the construction period', a term not defined, yet runs until the later of final completion and the end of the defects notification period. Whether obligations arising after the construction period, such as remedying defects in the defects notification period, are guaranteed is unclear.
rows.interim_handling: Execute Form 4-D in its issued wording, and brief the EPC parent on the wider reading (cover through the defects notification period) as its conservative exposure so that approvals are not delayed.
rows.practical_impact: The guarantee is executed and submitted in Envelope A (VOL-I 8.7, 9.1(d)); the EPC parent's approval of an unlimited guarantee depends on its scope, making this a critical-path signature item.
rows.proposed_question: Volume IV, Form 4-D, page 7, and Volume I, Clause 8.7, page 4: Form 4-D defines the guaranteed obligations as the EPC Contractor's obligations 'during the construction period' and provides for expiry on the later of the issue of the final completion certificate and the expiry of the defects notification period. When does the 'construction period' end for the purposes of Form 4-D, and do the guaranteed obligations include obligations of the EPC Contractor arising after the end of that period and before expiry, including during the defects notification period?
rows.sources: VOL-I:8.7 p4: “unconditional as to the EPC Contractor's obligations during the construction period”; VOL-IV:F4-D/guaranteed-obligations p7: “All obligations of the EPC Contractor under the EPC Contract during the construction period, including the payment of liquidated damages.”; VOL-IV:F4-D/expiry p7: “The later of the issue of the final completion certificate under the EPC Contract and the expiry of the defects notification period”; VOL-IV:F4-D/limit-of-liability p7: “Unlimited as to the guaranteed obligations”

rows.gap: The Works include 'the treated effluent storage reservoir', but Volume II gives no capacity, retention time, location or other requirement for it.
rows.interim_handling: Size the reservoir on a stated design-basis assumption linked to the Table 2-6 flows and carry a cost sensitivity; record it as a design assumption, not a qualification.
rows.practical_impact: Reservoir size is a capex item and affects how peak or storm treated flows are handled ahead of the transmission main; without a requirement, sizing is left to each Bidder and compliance cannot be checked.
rows.proposed_question: Volume II, Clause 1.2, page 2: The Works include 'the treated effluent storage reservoir', but no capacity or design requirement for it is stated in Volume II. What capacity and design criteria apply to the treated effluent storage reservoir, or is its sizing for the Bidder to determine?
rows.sources: VOL-II:1.2 p2: “the treated effluent transmission main; the treated effluent storage reservoir; and all associated electrical, control and civil works”

rows.already_settled: The Financial Model must be in Microsoft Excel format (VOL-I 10.3); that is not in question. Non-conforming names are corrected by the Authority at the Bidder's risk (Appendix 2).
rows.gap: The convention fixes a '.pdf' extension although the Financial Model must be an Excel file, and it does not define [BIDDER] or which date [YYYYMMDD] represents; [VOL] has no evident value for the Financial Model.
rows.interim_handling: Set up a configurable naming scheme: the printed pattern for PDF files, the same pattern with the native Excel extension for the model, one [BIDDER] code and one date value applied consistently, folder depth of three levels at most and names under 120 characters.
rows.practical_impact: Names must follow the convention 'strictly' (6.5); the responsiveness risk is low, but a misnamed Envelope B file could be mis-filed or misread in evaluation.
rows.proposed_question: Volume I, Appendix 2, page 7: The file naming convention ends in '.pdf', while Clause 10.3 (page 5) requires the Financial Model in Microsoft Excel format. How is the Financial Model file to be named under the convention, what should the [BIDDER] element contain, and which date should the [YYYYMMDD] element represent?
rows.sources: VOL-I:App2/para1 p7: “Files shall be named: ISTP2026-014_[BIDDER]_[ENV]_[VOL]_[NN]_[YYYYMMDD].pdf where [ENV] is A or B, [VOL] is the volume or form reference, and [NN] is a two-digit sequence.”; VOL-I:6.5 p3: “Electronic files shall be named strictly in accordance with the convention at Appendix 2.”; VOL-I:10.3 p5: “The Financial Model shall be submitted in unlocked, fully formula-linked Microsoft Excel format”

rows.already_settled: Section 2.2 settles that the Portal remains available on 22 November; VOL-I 8.1 settles that an unapproved change in composition results in rejection. Neither settles the deadline.
rows.clause: Sections 3.2 and 2.2; response to clarification request 17
rows.gap: Section 3.2 sets the deadline for applying for consent to admit the proposed O&M Operator as a member at four Working Days before the Proposal Due Date (Thursday 26 November 2026). Counting back with Sunday 22 November 2026 notified as a closure (Sections 2.1-2.2; VOL-I 2.4 as amended) gives Thursday 19 November 2026. The response to request 17 gives 'not later than Sunday 22 November 2026', the closure day itself (the Portal remains available). The Addendum does not say which date governs.
rows.interim_handling: Only if the O&M Operator is not a member: notify the intention by the earlier reading of Section 3.3 (Thursday 5 November 2026) and lodge the application by Thursday 19 November 2026, the earlier of the two dates; do not rely on Q17's later date unless the Authority confirms it by Addendum.
rows.practical_impact: Only for a Bidder whose O&M Operator is not a member. An application lodged between 20 and 22 November would be in time under Q17 but late under Section 3.2 read with the closure; without consent the admission is an unapproved change and the Proposal is rejected (VOL-I 8.1).
rows.proposed_question: Addendum No. 3, Section 3.2 (page 1) and the response to clarification request 17 (page 2): Section 3.2 requires an application for consent to the admission of the proposed O&M Operator not later than four (4) Working Days before the Proposal Due Date, which, with Sunday 22 November 2026 notified under Section 2.2 as a day on which the Authority's offices are closed, falls on Thursday 19 November 2026. The response to request 17 states 'not later than Sunday 22 November 2026'. Please confirm the date and time by which the application must be submitted through the Portal.
rows.sources: ADD-03:3.2 p1: “not later than four (4) Working Days before the Proposal Due Date”; ADD-03:Q17 p2: “shall be submitted through the Portal not later than Sunday 22 November 2026”; ADD-03:2.2 p1: “The Authority's offices will be closed on Sunday 22 November 2026. That day is notified for the purposes of Volume I Clause 2.4 as amended by Section 2.1.”; VOL-I:8.1 p4: “An unapproved change shall result in rejection of the Proposal.”

rows.already_settled: The operative provisions (2.1-2.2) notify the day for the purposes of VOL-I 2.4, and an Addendum's provisions prevail over its cover summary; the Proposal Due Date itself (Thursday 26 November 2026) does not move.
rows.clause: Cover and Sections 2.1-2.2 (with Volume I Clauses 2.4 and 5.2)
rows.gap: The cover says the closure does not affect any deadline, but Sections 2.1-2.2 make Sunday 22 November 2026 a day that is not a Working Day, which moves every Working-Day period running across it: the VOL-I 5.2 clarification cut-off becomes Wednesday 11 November 2026 (not Thursday 12 November) and Section 3.2 gives Thursday 19 November 2026. The cover is a summary, but it states the opposite of the operative provisions.
rows.interim_handling: Plan to the operative provisions (the earlier dates): clarification requests by Wednesday 11 November 2026; the Section 3.2 application by Thursday 19 November 2026. Because this question must itself be lodged before the cut-off, raise it early or not at all; the plan does not depend on the answer.
rows.practical_impact: A request lodged on 12 November in reliance on the cover would be late under VOL-I 5.2 as now counted and would not be answered; the same applies to any Working-Day deadline that spans 22 November.
rows.proposed_question: Addendum No. 3, cover and Sections 2.1-2.2 (page 1): the cover states that 'The closure of the Authority's offices does not affect any deadline under the RFP Documents', while Section 2.2 notifies Sunday 22 November 2026 for the purposes of Volume I Clause 2.4 as amended, so that it is not a Working Day. Please confirm whether Working-Day periods that run across 22 November 2026, including the clarification cut-off in Volume I Clause 5.2 (page 3) and the period in Section 3.2, exclude that day.
rows.sources: ADD-03:cover/para3 p1: “The closure of the Authority's offices does not affect any deadline under the RFP Documents.”; ADD-03:2.1 p1: “or a day notified by the Authority in an Addendum as a day on which its offices are closed”; ADD-03:2.2 p1: “That day is notified for the purposes of Volume I Clause 2.4 as amended by Section 2.1.”; VOL-I:5.2 p3: “Requests for clarification shall be submitted no later than ten (10) Working Days before the Proposal Due Date.”
